tour.name: 3-Day Private Cappadocia Tour: Cave Hotel, Valleys & Underground City
tour.subtitle: Three unhurried days in Cappadocia with a licensed guide and private car: sleep two nights in a cave hotel in Göreme, watch the balloons rise at dawn, walk Rose Valley at sunset, see the painted rock churches of Göreme, the fairy chimneys of Paşabağ and descend into the underground city of Kaymaklı.

highlights: Two nights in a cave hotel in Göreme
The balloons rising over the valleys at dawn
Frescoed rock churches of the Göreme Open Air Museum
The fairy chimneys of Paşabağ and Devrent
Eight levels deep: Kaymaklı underground city
Airport transfers, guide, car, hotel and lunches included
tour.overview:
Cappadocia is a landscape shaped by fire and water. Millions of years ago, volcanoes such as Erciyes and Hasan covered the plateau in thick layers of ash that hardened into soft tuff; wind and rain have since carved it into valleys of cones, pillars and 'fairy chimneys' with caps of harder rock. People have been hollowing out this stone for thousands of years – early Christians cut churches and monasteries into the cliffs and painted them with frescoes, and whole towns dug underground cities to hide from raiders. The Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985.

A day trip only scratches the surface. This private three-day tour gives you time to live in the landscape: two nights in a cave hotel in Göreme, the dawn sky full of balloons, the best valleys at the best light, and the main sites with a licensed guide but without the rush. You visit Uçhisar castle and Pigeon Valley on arrival and walk Rose Valley at sunset. The next day takes you to the painted churches of the Göreme Open Air Museum, the fairy chimneys of Paşabağ and Devrent, and the potters of Avanos. On the last morning you descend into Kaymaklı underground city and explore the cave villages of Çavuşin and Ortahisar before your transfer to the airport.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
• Start: Kayseri or Nevşehir airport, or your hotel in Cappadocia
• End: Kayseri or Nevşehir airport
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver; 2 nights in a cave hotel with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, hotel and final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; valley walks of 2 to 4 km on dirt paths

WHAT YOU SEE
• Uçhisar castle and Pigeon Valley.
• Rose Valley at sunset.
• The Göreme Open Air Museum.
• Paşabağ (Monks Valley) and Devrent (Imagination Valley).
• Avanos and its pottery workshops.
• Kaymaklı underground city.
• Çavuşin old village and Ortahisar.

WHY THIS WORKS
Staying in Göreme puts you in the middle of the valleys: you can step out onto the terrace at dawn to watch the balloons, and every site is 10 to 30 minutes away, so the days are full but never rushed.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, families, photographers and anyone who wants to experience Cappadocia properly between Istanbul and the coast.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you only have one day, choose our Red Tour or Green Tour. For a whole-country trip, see our 8-day Turkey highlights tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The balloon flight is not included because places and weather vary: we can book it for you on the morning of day 2 (or day 3 as a back-up). Nights are cool even in summer, and winters are cold and often snowy. Wear good shoes for the valley paths.

days.name: Arrival, Uçhisar castle, Pigeon Valley and Rose Valley at sunset
days.description:
What to expect: airport welcome, check-in at your cave hotel in Göreme, the panoramic heights of Uçhisar and a sunset walk through Rose Valley.

Your guide and driver meet you at Kayseri airport (about 1 hour 15 minutes from Göreme) or Nevşehir airport (about 45 minutes), or at your hotel if you arrive by bus. On the way, the guide explains how the volcanoes on the horizon created the landscape you are about to see. After checking in to your cave hotel in Göreme and having lunch, you drive to Uçhisar, a village built around a huge rock riddled with rooms and passages, the highest point in the region. From the top you see the whole of central Cappadocia, with Mount Erciyes on the horizon on clear days.

Below Uçhisar lies Pigeon Valley, named after the thousands of dovecotes carved into its walls; for centuries the villagers collected pigeon droppings to fertilise vineyards and orchards. You walk part of the valley path or enjoy it from the viewpoint, then continue to Çavuşin and the head of Rose Valley. In the late afternoon you set off on an easy walk of about 3 km through the valley, past hidden rock churches and pink and orange cliffs that glow at sunset. The walk ends at a viewpoint where you watch the sun go down over the valleys, and your driver takes you back to Göreme for a free evening.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
11:00 – Meeting at the airport or your hotel.
12:30 – Check-in at your cave hotel in Göreme, then lunch.
14:30 – Uçhisar castle.
15:30 – Pigeon Valley viewpoint.
16:30 – Rose Valley walk (about 3 km, 1 hour 30 minutes).
18:00 – Sunset at the viewpoint, return to Göreme.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If your flight lands later, we start with lunch and adjust the afternoon.
• Rose Valley paths are dusty or muddy depending on the season; wear trainers or walking shoes.
• Sunset time varies from about 16:45 in December to about 20:30 in June.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, private car and driver, licensed guide, lunch, Uçhisar castle ticket, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: cave hotel in Göreme.
Meals: lunch.

days.name: Balloons at dawn, Göreme Open Air Museum, Paşabağ, Devrent and Avanos
days.description:
What to expect: the balloons at sunrise, the frescoed churches of Göreme, the most famous fairy chimneys and the potters of Avanos.

If you have booked a balloon flight, you are collected before dawn and drift over the valleys for about an hour as the sun rises, then celebrate with a glass of juice or sparkling wine on landing. If not, step out onto your hotel terrace: on calm mornings dozens of balloons rise around Göreme, one of the great sights of Turkey. After breakfast your guide meets you at about 9:00.

The Göreme Open Air Museum is a monastic complex of rock-cut churches, chapels and refectories used from the 10th to the 12th centuries. Your guide explains the frescoes – scenes from the life of Christ in bright blues and reds – and how the monks lived, ate and prayed in the rock. The Dark Church (separate ticket) has some of the best-preserved paintings in Cappadocia because so little light reaches them. Across the road, the Tokalı Church, with its deep blue walls, is included in the main ticket.

You continue to Paşabağ, also called Monks Valley, where fairy chimneys with two or three caps stand like giant mushrooms; one of them holds the cell of a hermit dedicated to Saint Simeon. Next is Devrent, or Imagination Valley, where you search the pink rocks for shapes such as the famous camel. After lunch you drive to Avanos on the Red River (Kızılırmak), where potters have used its red clay since the Hittites; you watch a master throw a pot on a kick wheel and may try it yourself. You return to Göreme in the late afternoon.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:00 – Optional balloon flight (pick-up from your hotel).
09:00 – Departure with your guide.
09:15 – Göreme Open Air Museum (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
11:00 – Paşabağ (Monks Valley).
12:00 – Devrent (Imagination Valley).
13:00 – Lunch in Avanos.
14:30 – Pottery workshop in Avanos.
16:00 – Return to Göreme; free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Balloon flights depend on the weather and are decided by the civil aviation authority each morning; if the flight is cancelled, we try again on day 3.
• There is no obligation to buy at the pottery workshop.
• You can add a Turkish night show or a sunset horse ride on request.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets to the Göreme Open Air Museum and Paşabağ, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: balloon flight, Dark Church ticket, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: cave hotel in Göreme.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Kaymaklı underground city, Ortahisar, Çavuşin and departure
days.description:
What to expect: a descent into an underground city, two cave villages and your transfer to the airport.

After breakfast and check-out, you drive about 20 minutes south to Kaymaklı, one of the largest underground cities in Cappadocia. Its tunnels were probably begun in the Phrygian period and greatly extended in Byzantine times, when villagers sheltered here from raids with their animals and food for weeks at a time. You walk through narrow passages and down to the lower levels, past stables, kitchens blackened by smoke, wine presses, chapels and ventilation shafts, and see the great rolling stone doors that could be closed from inside.

Back in the daylight, you visit Ortahisar, a quiet village around a tall rock castle, where farmers still store lemons, oranges and potatoes in cool caves dug into the hillsides. You then go to Çavuşin, where the old village climbs a cliff full of abandoned cave houses below the Church of Saint John the Baptist, one of the oldest in the region. After a farewell lunch with a view of Love Valley and its tall pillars, you are driven to Kayseri or Nevşehir airport for your onward flight.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:00 – Back-up balloon morning if day 2 was cancelled.
09:00 – Check-out and departure.
09:30 – Kaymaklı underground city (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
11:15 – Ortahisar village and castle viewpoint.
12:15 – Çavuşin old village.
13:00 – Lunch with a view of Love Valley.
14:30 – Transfer to the airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Kaymaklı passages are low and narrow in places; anyone who is claustrophobic can stay on the upper level.
• Choose a flight after 16:30 from Kayseri or after 16:00 from Nevşehir; we adjust the day to earlier flights.
• Derinkuyu, a deeper underground city, can replace Kaymaklı on request.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Kaymaklı ticket, lunch, bottled water, airport transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: flights, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, the hotel and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the balloon flight included?
faq.answer: No, because prices change with the season and flights depend on the weather. We can book a standard or deluxe flight for you on day 2, with day 3 as a back-up, and add it to your confirmation.

faq.question: What kind of hotel will we stay in?
faq.answer: A boutique cave hotel in Göreme with rooms carved into the rock, private bathrooms and a terrace for watching the balloons. The price is based on double or twin rooms; single rooms and upgrades are available.

faq.question: Which airport should we fly into?
faq.answer: Kayseri (ASR) has more flights from Istanbul; Nevşehir (NAV) is closer. Both are included. We can also meet you at the bus station or your hotel.

faq.question: Can we start in Istanbul?
faq.answer: The tour starts in Cappadocia. Flights from Istanbul take about 1 hour 20 minutes, and we can help you choose times that fit the programme.

faq.question: Are dinners included?
faq.answer: No, so you can try the restaurants of Göreme freely. Your guide will recommend places for testi kebab, cooked in a sealed clay pot, and other local dishes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the underground city, the cave rooms and the balloons. The valley walks can be shortened or replaced by viewpoints.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Viewpoints and villages are easy to reach by car, but the Open Air Museum has steps and the underground city has low, narrow passages.

faq.question: What is the weather like?
faq.answer: Summers are hot and dry by day and cool at night. Spring and autumn are mild. Winters are cold, often below zero, with snow that makes the valleys beautiful.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only the pottery workshop in Avanos, which is a cultural visit with no obligation to buy. There are no carpet or jewellery stops unless you ask.

faq.question: Can we extend the tour?
faq.answer: Yes. A fourth day can add the Green Tour with Ihlara Valley and Selime Monastery, or a full day of hiking.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to November for mild weather and frequent balloon flights. Winter has fewer flights but very few visitors.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 7 days before the tour starts. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
